clue.text: Jug son lifts

parts.note: jug and nick are both slang for prison
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy hoists a jug, perhaps to drink from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug looks like a container or a verb; here it is slang for jail, as is nick.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and lifts is another informal verb for stealing.

clue.text: Drunk causes inn problems

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunkard makes trouble at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuisances are annoyances or irritations, and problems is a broad synonym for those.

clue.text: Short policeman twice seen with a drink

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
the shortened policeman repeated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short police officer is twice spotted having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like a description of the officer's height, but it trims a letter from the word for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Unusual loose garments male's removed

indicators.note: loose means not held in place, so these letters are free to move around
removed means taken away, so that one letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: It is odd that a man has taken off his loose-fitting clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose seems to describe the clothes, but it signals the mix; the M for male comes out first.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unusual are synonyms for something odd or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: What Trump does? Deteriorates

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Judd Trump is a snooker champion, and a snooker player sends balls into the pockets
second meaning: an idiom for falling into ruin or decline

explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at a well-known politician, but this Trump is the English snooker player Judd Trump; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something sliding into neglect and ruin, which is exactly what deteriorating means.

clue.text: Outbursts about European visitors

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around a letter

parts.note: a gust is a sudden outburst, of wind or feeling
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Tourists from the continent complain loudly about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests are people invited or staying somewhere, which makes them visitors.

clue.text: Recording English gang underneath hospital department

indicators.note: in a down answer, underneath means placed below, so these come after what follows them in the clue

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
E is the abbreviation for English
a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: A ward clerk notes that an English gang is operating beneath a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering data in a ledger is recording it, so the two present participles match.

clue.text: Just the same, tense pondering

parts.note: though can mean nevertheless, just the same
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone still remains anxious while mulling something over.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective for anxious, but it is the grammar term abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought as a noun is the act of reflection, which is what pondering is as a gerund.

clue.text: In favour of new big cat, say

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
N is the abbreviation for new
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: Someone backs a newly arrived big cat and has their say on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Say at the end looks like 'for example', but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare or utter something, which is to say it.

clue.text: Italian restaurant rejected small items of pastry

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An Italian eatery sends back its little pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: Small seems to describe the pastries but it gives the plural ending S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are pastry cases with a filling, so each is an item of pastry.

clue.text: Wrong concert I broadcast, entertaining head of radio

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone, so the scrambled letters take a guest inside them
to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of radio

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a concert they put out on air went wrong while featuring a radio boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect and wrong are plain synonyms for something not right or accurate.

clue.text: Reported river smell

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the river

parts.note: the Oder is a river forming part of the border between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: News of a stinking river reaches the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or whiff, the noun sense of smell.

clue.text: Touching stove with hot stew, dropping half

indicators.note: dropping half means losing two of the word's four letters, keeping only its front part

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of cast-iron kitchen range
hot and in both mean fashionable
the first half of stew

explanation.surface: A cook's stew is reduced by half while bubbling on a hot stove.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot sounds like the stove's temperature, but it gives IN in the sense of trendy. An Aga is a heavy British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaning against a wall is touching it, so the preposition matches that physical-contact sense.

clue.text: South African country, in retrospect, contains old districts

indicators.note: looking in retrospect means looking backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: contains says the backwards string holds another letter inside it

parts.note: Niger is a West African state
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Looking back, a southern African nation is said to include ancient districts.
explanation.walkthrough: South African looks like one phrase for a nationality, but South gives a single letter and the country is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions are areas or zones of a country, which is what districts are.

clue.text: Mentions crossing India's large urban areas

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across and around, so one word straddles a letter

parts.note: to cite is to mention or quote
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone notes how India's big conurbations are crossing paths.
explanation.definitionFit: Cities are by definition large towns, i.e. sizeable built-up urban places.

clue.text: Runs inside tent mate assembled for medical care

indicators.note: inside places one letter within the rearranged ones
assembled means put together from parts, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A camper's companion puts together a first-aid post inside the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical attention given to a patient, which is what care means here.

clue.text: One with initially negative attitude, for example

definitions.note: the phrase stands for 'for instance', so the definition is loose

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of negative
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A person who starts out with a pessimistic outlook is offered as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase: 'for example' and 'for instance' are interchangeable, so the setter treats the answer as their key word.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example or case, as in the stock phrase where the two words swap freely.

clue.text: Articulates urge admitted by former lovers

indicators.note: to be admitted by someone is to be let inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: exes are former partners
to press is to urge strongly

explanation.surface: Former partners confess to a lingering desire.
explanation.walkthrough: Admitted reads as confessed, but it means let in.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, which is to articulate it.

clue.text: Appropriate American's upset by international data chart

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: US abbreviates American
I is the abbreviation for international
a table lays out data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: An American gets annoyed by a chart of global statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable means fitting or right for the purpose, the adjective sense of appropriate.

clue.text: Religious group going round Portugal with odd compass

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so one word wraps around a letter

parts.note: a sect is a religious faction
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
rum is old British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A band of believers travels around Portugal carrying a peculiar navigational compass.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass is not the direction-finder but the noun meaning range or extent; rum as odd is a dated Britishism.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass in the sense of scope or range matches a spectrum, the full range of something.

clue.text: Consume second bit of grass in the field

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the second bit of a word is its second letter

parts.note: the second letter of grass
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: An animal grazes on grass out in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Field reads as a pasture, but it is the definition: a theatre of war is a field of operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is an area of activity, as in a theatre of war, which is a field of operations.

clue.text: Bruce, maybe bitten by snake, becomes comatose

indicators.note: something bitten is held between the jaws, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Bruce Lee, the martial arts star, is an example of someone surnamed Lee

explanation.surface: A man called Bruce suffers a snakebite and falls into a coma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that Bruce is one example of a Lee, so the answer needs his surname rather than his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone comatose is deeply unconscious, and asleep is a looser synonym for that unresponsive state.

clue.text: This writer is gripped by ogre's piercing screams

indicators.note: something gripped is held tight inside, so one letter sits within another word

parts.note: Shrek is the ogre of the animated films
the writer of the clue refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The writer, held by an ogre, lets out shrill cries.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieks are high-pitched cries, so they are piercing screams.

clue.text: Somewhat regularly sail a route, possessing craft

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so one word keeps another inside it

parts.note: to ply a route is to travel it regularly
art and craft both mean skill

explanation.surface: A boat makes a fairly regular run along its route.
explanation.walkthrough: Regularly looks like a signal for alternate letters, but here it belongs to the phrase for ply; craft is skill, not a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means to some degree, and somewhat is an adverb with that same limited sense.

clue.text: Following funny taste, finally reject most stout

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: funny means peculiar or out of the ordinary, so these letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of reject

explanation.surface: Someone with a peculiar palate ends up turning down the strongest stout beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the dark beer, but it is the adjective for plump; the final letter of reject joins taste before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout as an adjective means plump or heavy, so the superlative most stout equals the fattest.

clue.text: Set up game of billiards?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to incriminate someone falsely
second meaning: a single game in snooker or billiards

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like arranging a game; the question mark marks the cue-sport sense as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame someone is to fake evidence against them, and a frame is also one unit of play in cue sports.

clue.text: Sort out a Republican row

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a range is a line or row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A political argument involving a Republican needs settling.
explanation.walkthrough: Row reads as a quarrel (rhymes with cow), but here it is a line of things (rhymes with go).
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to put them in order, which is a plain sense of sort out.

clue.text: Sound from piano is excruciating, to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent means only partly, so the answer is a portion of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across piano, is and excruciating

explanation.surface: The playing coming out of the piano is somewhat painful to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Forestall State Department's conclusion

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter, so only that one letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of department

explanation.surface: A government office is trying to head off the outcome of a policy.
explanation.walkthrough: State Department reads as the US foreign ministry, but State is a verb here and Department only lends its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to prevent or ward it off in advance, which is what forestall means.

clue.text: Power sources hit by current energy setbacks, primarily

parts.note: to batter is to strike repeatedly
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the leading letters of the words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Electrical supplies suffer from current surges and energy failures.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface makes current read as a flow of power; it supplies I, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Batteries store chemical energy and supply electricity, so they are portable sources of power.

clue.text: Very old Tango merely effervescent

parts.note: ex- means former or old

indicators.note: something effervescent fizzes and bubbles, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old fizzy drink called Tango has gone flat and is only slightly bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is also a British brand of fizzy orange drink, which is what the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely and very are both intensifying adverbs meaning to a high degree.

clue.text: Looks for submissive maiden abandoned in ship

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the letters for a vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: meek means docile or submissive
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a shy young woman left behind on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden suggests a young woman, but it is the cricket term, abbreviated M; removing it from the word for submissive leaves the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek something is to search or look for it.
